intro: Calculate sq ft to acres accurately for residential house lots, commercial parcels, landscaping plans, and land surveys. By exact statutory definition, 1 acre equals 43,560 square feet (66 ft × 660 ft, or 1 chain by 1 furlong), which makes 1 square foot equal to 0.00002296 acres. Divide any square footage by 43,560 to get acreage, or inspect common lot sizes from 1 ft² to 435,600 ft² below—including quarter-acre and half-acre benchmarks.
alsoWrittenAs: sq ft to acres, sq ft to ac, ft² to ac, square footage to acres, sq. ft. to acres

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: 'Square Acre' Misnomer & International vs. US Survey Foot
items: An acre is already a unit of area (43,560 ft²), so 'square acre' is a common misnomer. If you want to go in the opposite direction—converting acres to square feet—tap Swap or use our Acres to Square Feet converter.

Legacy land deeds occasionally reference the US survey acre (retired by NIST at the end of 2022). The difference between the international acre and US survey acre is under 0.18 ft² per acre (~4 parts per million), negligible for real estate listings but worth checking on historic state-plane surveys.

faqs.question: How many square feet are in half an acre?
faqs.answer: Half an acre equals exactly 21,780 square feet (0.5 × 43,560 ft²). If the lot were a perfect square, each side would measure about 147.58 feet.

faqs.question: What is the square footage of a quarter acre?
faqs.answer: A quarter acre (0.25 ac) equals exactly 10,890 square feet (0.25 × 43,560 ft²)—for example, a rectangular lot measuring 90 ft × 121 ft.

faqs.question: How many acres is 10,000 square feet?
faqs.answer: 10,000 square feet equals 0.22957 acres (10,000 ÷ 43,560), which is slightly less than a quarter acre (0.25 ac = 10,890 ft²).

faqs.question: What is the sq footage in 1 acre?
faqs.answer: There are exactly 43,560 square feet in 1 acre. A square 1-acre parcel measures approximately 208.71 feet on each side.
